outputs.L3:
A gas turbine engine includes a fan having a plurality of fan blades configured to rotate about an engine axis. The fan is positioned upstream of a core flow path and is arranged to drive air into the engine during operation. A portion of the air may enter the core flow path, while another portion may pass through a bypass flow path surrounding the core.

The engine further includes an on-wing portion having a compressor section and a combustor. The compressor section is arranged to receive and compress air flowing through the core flow path. The combustor is in fluid communication with the compressor section and is configured to receive the compressed air, mix it with fuel, and generate high-energy combustion gases.

A turbine section is positioned downstream of, and in fluid communication with, the combustor. The turbine section receives the combustion gases from the combustor and extracts energy from the gases to produce rotational power. The turbine section is coupled to a fan drive gear system module, which is configured to transmit torque and rotate the fan about the engine axis.

The gas turbine engine also includes a connector assembly that secures the on-wing portion of the engine to the fan drive gear system module. The connector assembly includes first and second removable members that cooperate to form a detachable connection between these engine portions. This arrangement allows the fan drive gear system module and the on-wing portion to be joined during assembly and separated when maintenance, repair, or replacement is required.

The first and second removable members are fastened together by a plurality of fasteners that extend generally radially relative to the engine axis. These radially extending fasteners are positioned so that they are accessible through the bypass flow path. As a result, service personnel may access and remove the fasteners without requiring extensive disassembly of surrounding engine structures, thereby facilitating installation, inspection, and maintenance of the connector assembly.
outputs.L4:
A gas turbine engine is provided with a modular arrangement that allows a fan drive gear system to be installed, removed, or serviced with improved accessibility. The engine includes a fan section, a compressor section, a combustor section, and a turbine section arranged along an engine central longitudinal axis. A bypass flow path is defined radially outward of a core engine flow path, and airflow from the fan is directed through the bypass flow path during operation.

The fan drive gear system module is operatively coupled to the turbine section so that rotational energy produced by the turbine section can be transmitted through the gear system to drive the fan section at a desired speed. The module may include a gear train, support structure, bearings, lubrication features, and associated housings or carriers. The gear system allows the fan to rotate at a speed different from that of the turbine shaft, improving engine efficiency and performance.

The fan drive gear system module is removably connected to an on-wing portion of the gas turbine engine by a connector assembly. The connector assembly includes a plurality of fasteners that extend generally radially with respect to the engine central longitudinal axis. These fasteners secure the fan drive gear system module to adjacent engine structure during normal operation, while also allowing the module to be detached when maintenance, inspection, repair, or replacement is required.

The radially extending fasteners are positioned so that they are accessible through the bypass flow path. This arrangement permits maintenance personnel to reach and remove the fasteners without requiring complete removal of the engine from the aircraft wing. As a result, the fan drive gear system module may be separated from the on-wing engine portion more efficiently than in configurations where the connecting hardware is hidden or accessible only after significant engine disassembly.

In use, the connector assembly maintains the fan drive gear system module in proper alignment with the turbine section and fan section while transmitting operational loads through the engine structure. When servicing is required, access panels, nacelle structures, or other surrounding components may be opened or removed to expose the bypass flow path. The radially extending fasteners can then be loosened or removed through the bypass flow path, allowing the fan drive gear system module to be disconnected from the on-wing engine portion.

This modular design reduces maintenance time and complexity, particularly for geared turbofan engines in which the fan drive gear system is a critical and high-value component. By enabling the fan drive gear system module to be removed while the engine remains installed on the aircraft, the design can reduce aircraft downtime, simplify field service procedures, and lower overall maintenance costs.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays a very important role. It is called the definite article, and we use it when we are talking about something specific or already known. For example, saying “the book” means a particular book, not just any book.

This simple word helps give clarity and meaning to sentences. Without “the,” English would often sound incomplete or confusing. Compare “I saw dog” with “I saw the dog.” The second sentence tells us that the speaker is referring to a specific dog.

“The” also appears in many famous titles and expressions, such as *The Bible*, *The Great Gatsby*, and *the best*. It can make something feel important, unique, or familiar.

Although it is short and easy to overlook, “the” is one of the most common and useful words in English. It shows that even the smallest words can have a big impact on communication.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a gas turbine engine with a fan drive gear system module removably connected to an on-wing portion using radially extending fasteners accessible through the bypass flow path.
counterfactuals.output: A gas turbine engine includes an on-wing portion having a fan section, a compressor section, a combustor section, and a turbine section arranged about an engine longitudinal axis. A fan drive gear system module is removably connected to the on-wing portion and is configured to transmit torque between a turbine-driven shaft and a fan rotor. The fan drive gear system module includes a gear system housing and a plurality of mounting features circumferentially distributed about the engine longitudinal axis. The gear system housing is secured to a corresponding support structure of the on-wing portion by a plurality of fasteners extending generally radially relative to the engine longitudinal axis. The fasteners are accessible from a bypass flow path of the gas turbine engine to permit installation and removal of the fan drive gear system module while at least part of the on-wing portion remains installed on an aircraft. The arrangement enables modular servicing or replacement of the fan drive gear system with reduced disassembly of surrounding engine structure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical patent claim summary for a geared turbofan engine including a fan, compressor, combustor, turbine section, core nacelle, and connector assembly between the engine core and fan drive gear module.
counterfactuals.output:
A geared turbofan engine is disclosed comprising a fan section, a compressor section, a combustor, a turbine section, a core nacelle, a fan drive gear module, and a connector assembly arranged between an engine core and the fan drive gear module.

In one aspect, the engine includes a fan rotatable about an engine central longitudinal axis and configured to deliver a bypass airflow through a bypass duct. A compressor section is disposed downstream of the fan and includes at least one compressor rotor configured to compress a core airflow. A combustor is positioned downstream of the compressor section and arranged to receive the compressed core airflow and generate combustion gases. A turbine section is disposed downstream of the combustor and includes at least one turbine rotor configured to extract energy from the combustion gases to drive the compressor section and the fan through a fan drive gear module.

The fan drive gear module is coupled between a turbine-driven shaft and the fan and is configured to provide a speed reduction between the turbine-driven shaft and the fan. The engine core is at least partially surrounded by a core nacelle defining an exterior boundary of the core flowpath and at least a portion of the bypass duct.

A connector assembly is provided between the engine core and the fan drive gear module. The connector assembly is configured to mechanically couple and support the fan drive gear module relative to the engine core while accommodating operational loads generated during engine operation. The connector assembly may include one or more structural members extending between a stationary engine-core structure and a housing or support structure of the fan drive gear module. The connector assembly is configured to transfer at least one of axial loads, radial loads, torque reaction loads, bending loads, or vibratory loads between the fan drive gear module and the engine core.

In certain embodiments, the connector assembly is positioned within or adjacent to the core nacelle and is arranged to maintain alignment of the fan drive gear module with the engine central longitudinal axis. The connector assembly may include a plurality of circumferentially spaced connectors, struts, links, brackets, flanges, mounts, or support arms. The connector assembly may further include compliant or flexible features configured to permit limited relative thermal or mechanical displacement between the fan drive gear module and the engine core while maintaining structural support.

In another aspect, the connector assembly is configured to interface with a gear module housing and a core structural case, such as a compressor case, intermediate case, fan frame, or bearing support structure. The connector assembly may be removable or modular to facilitate installation, servicing, or replacement of the fan drive gear module. The arrangement provides improved load transfer, gear module support, alignment control, and integration between the engine core and the geared fan drive system in a geared turbofan architecture.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal aerospace patent paragraph about a gas turbine engine architecture where first and second connector members attach an on-wing portion to a fan drive gear system module with removable radial fasteners.
counterfactuals.output: In one embodiment, a gas turbine engine includes a fan section, a core engine section, and a fan drive gear system module disposed to transmit torque between a turbine-driven shaft and a fan rotor. An on-wing portion of the engine is configured to remain installed relative to an aircraft nacelle or pylon during removal of the fan drive gear system module. A first connector member is secured to the on-wing portion and a second connector member is secured to the fan drive gear system module, the first and second connector members defining complementary radial attachment interfaces. A plurality of removable radial fasteners extend through the first and second connector members in a generally radial direction relative to an engine central longitudinal axis to releasably couple the fan drive gear system module to the on-wing portion. Upon removal of the radial fasteners, the fan drive gear system module is separable from the on-wing portion as a unit without requiring removal of the on-wing portion from the engine installation, thereby facilitating modular maintenance, inspection, or replacement of the fan drive gear system while maintaining structural alignment between the fan drive gear system module and the remaining gas turbine engine architecture.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in patent language, an aircraft gas turbine engine having a modular fan drive gear system coupled to the turbine section and secured to the engine by fasteners accessible from the bypass duct.
counterfactuals.output:
An aircraft gas turbine engine comprising a core engine, a fan section, a bypass duct, a turbine section, and a modular fan drive gear system operatively coupled between the turbine section and the fan section. The turbine section is configured to drive the fan section through the modular fan drive gear system at a reduced fan rotational speed relative to a turbine output rotational speed.

The modular fan drive gear system is disposed radially inward of the bypass duct and includes a gear module housing enclosing a gear train. The gear train may include an input member driven by the turbine section, an output member coupled to a fan shaft, and at least one intermediate gear element configured to transmit torque between the input member and the output member. The gear module housing defines a structural interface configured to mount the modular fan drive gear system to a static engine structure.

The modular fan drive gear system is removably secured to the aircraft gas turbine engine by a plurality of fasteners extending through the structural interface. The plurality of fasteners are positioned and oriented such that fastener heads, nuts, or tool-engagement portions thereof are accessible from the bypass duct. The bypass duct thereby provides a service access path for installation, removal, inspection, or replacement of the modular fan drive gear system without requiring disassembly of the core engine or removal of the turbine section.

In one embodiment, the static engine structure includes a fan frame, intermediate case, bearing support, or other annular support member disposed adjacent the gear module housing. The structural interface of the gear module housing includes a flange, lug arrangement, or annular mounting feature aligned with a corresponding mounting feature of the static engine structure. The plurality of fasteners extend through the aligned mounting features and clamp the gear module housing to the static engine structure.

In another embodiment, at least a portion of the fasteners are arranged circumferentially about an engine central longitudinal axis and are accessible through the bypass duct after removal of one or more bypass duct panels, fan duct liners, access doors, or other service openings. The fasteners may be oriented generally radially, axially, or obliquely relative to the engine central longitudinal axis to permit engagement by a tool inserted through the bypass duct.

The modular fan drive gear system may be configured as a unitized cartridge including the gear train, one or more bearings, lubrication passages, seals, and the gear module housing. The unitized cartridge is removable as a module after decoupling the input member from the turbine section, decoupling the output member from the fan section, and releasing the plurality of bypass-duct-accessible fasteners.

Accordingly, the aircraft gas turbine engine provides a serviceable geared fan architecture in which the fan drive gear system is structurally mounted to the engine and selectively removable via fasteners accessible from the bypass duct, thereby facilitating maintenance and replacement of the gear system while reducing engine teardown requirements.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
